_comment_1: ATOMIC GRANULARITY ONLY. One row per requirement, not per chapter. A 14-day project should produce on the order of 100 rows. If your row count is implausibly low for project age, the loop will self-terminate before the product is good. This is the Flatline failure mode.
_comment_2: Allowed status values: not_started | partial | done | deprecated. Every row should carry implementationRefs and testRefs once status >= partial. followupRefs link to F-NNN entries in FOLLOWUPS.md. A row marked status=deprecated stays in the ledger for institutional memory but no implementation or tests are owed; add a note in the row explaining what removed it from scope (slice id, Q-NNN resolution, etc.).

rows.requirement: Timeline persistence: actions performed during a time period are recorded and replay as a permanent past instance whenever another instance witnesses that period from outside it.
rows.note: Per-tick input recording buffer captures keyboard state plus normalized time-of-day each fixed step. A ghost capsule (`createGhost`) drains a frozen recording back into a separate Rapier dynamic capsule body tick-for-tick, integrated through the same fixed-step physics loop as the active player. `wireTraversal` (`src/sim/portalTraversal.ts`) now snapshots the active player's lifetime recording onto a ghost on every lit-portal entry and resets the recorder to a fresh buffer keyed at tick 0 of the destination timeline; the ghost spawns at the lifetime's start position with the lifetime's `originNormalized` as its tint. Still partial because per-timeline indexing of recordings (a ghost should only be visible in the timeline it was recorded in) is not yet implemented: the current slice keeps every spawned ghost alive in every timeline.

rows.requirement: Past instances replay recorded input frame-exact and cannot be altered, only worked around or physically redirected.
rows.note: End-to-end ghost replay landed: `createGhost` builds a Three.js mesh + Rapier dynamic capsule whose `advanceTick()` writes `replayAtTick(recording, tickIndex)` onto the body's planar velocity each fixed step, preserving y so gravity is not overwritten. The recording itself is deeply frozen at snapshot time so it cannot be mutated after capture. Past the end of the recording the ghost writes a zero planar velocity each tick and decelerates to a stop under the same linear damping as the active player. The ghost is a dynamic body with the same capsule collider as the player so it can be physically redirected (worked around) but not altered. `applyInstanceTint` stamps each ghost with its origin-time color so the player can read which timeline a ghost came from.

rows.requirement: Traveling through a portal does not erase the prior timeline; the entered instance continues to exist as a recorded instance in the timeline left behind.
rows.note: `wireTraversal` (`src/sim/portalTraversal.ts`) snapshots the active player's lifetime recording on every lit-portal entry and spawns a ghost replaying the snapshot from the lifetime's start position. The ghost persists after traversal so the path the player walked in the timeline being LEFT BEHIND is preserved as a permanent past instance. Still partial because the ghost is currently visible in every timeline (per-timeline indexing of recordings lands later, alongside REQ-007 instance generation numbering); a ghost recorded at 5:00 should only be visible when the player is back at 5:00.

rows.requirement: System enforces the no-paradox invariant: a player cannot prevent themselves from having done something they already did.
Portals have fixed locations and fixed destinations; a given door always leads to the same other time.
rows.note: Portal data model lands in `src/sim/portal.ts`. `createPortal({ door, destinationHours, isLit })` returns a frozen object with `readonly destinationHours` so the destination cannot mutate at runtime. Validation rejects non-finite destinations and destinations outside `[0, 24)` so callers downstream can trust the range. `createActOnePortals(doors)` produces the canonical four-door Act 1 configuration (South lit -> 12:00, East lit -> 6:00, North dark, West dark) and `src/scene/room.ts` consumes it at room build time. Still partial because the door MESH locations are placeholders sized for the prototype; a later slice will tie them to the room's actual collision geometry, and the runtime traversal half (REQ-009 send-the-player) is not yet implemented.

rows.requirement: An unvisited future contains no recorded events and no instances; a time period only contains events once an instance has entered it.
Instance generation numbering tracks generations from the original spawn (You1, You-1, You-2, ...).
Player input always controls the most recently spawned active instance.
A lit door is enterable and sends the player to the door's fixed destination time.
rows.note: End-to-end traversal lands in `src/sim/portalTraversal.ts`. `wireTraversal` subscribes to the `PortalTriggerSet` from PR #14, filters `enter` events on `isLit(portal)`, and on each lit entry: snapshots the active player's lifetime recorder onto a ghost spawned at the lifetime's start position with the lifetime's `originNormalized` as the tint (so the ghost belongs to the timeline being LEFT BEHIND), teleports the active player to the destination spawn pose (room center default; pluggable via `resolveSpawnPose` for per-time spawn poses in the next slice), zeros the player's velocity, re-stamps `player.originNormalized` and the player mesh tint via `applyInstanceTint(destinationNormalized)` (REQ-030), and opens a fresh `InputRecorder` keyed at tick 0 of the destination timeline. Dark portals are filtered (REQ-010). `src/app.ts` constructs an `ActiveLifetime` next to the player and wires the traversal handler; the per-fixed-step recording call resolves against the lifetime's current recorder so a swap on traversal does not require re-binding. The destination spawn pose detail (per-time spawn poses authored from the GDD's Act 1 anchors at 5:00 and 6:00) lands as REQ-013/REQ-014 in the next slice; the resolver hook is in place for that slice to drop in a real lookup.

rows.requirement: A dark door is a spawn-only exit; instances emerge from it and the player cannot enter.
rows.note: Dark portal half of the data model lands in `src/sim/portal.ts`. The Act 1 canonical table marks North and West dark per the GDD; `applyDoorLitState(door, false)` stamps the dark visual (near-black diffuse, no emissive). `wireTraversal` (`src/sim/portalTraversal.ts`) filters `enter` events on `isLit(portal)`, so dark portals do NOT teleport the player or spawn a ghost; this enforces the 'player cannot enter' half of REQ-010. Still partial because the spawn-only-emergence runtime half (instances actually emerging from dark doors when arriving from a recorded timeline) lands later, alongside per-timeline indexing.

rows.requirement: Door lit-versus-dark state is computed from arriving instances in the recorded timeline, not stored as a discoverable variable.
Act 1 cinematic at 12:00: two figures drag a knocked-out body through the North door to the center of the room, then fade to black.
Act 1 spawn at 5:00: the player stands in the center of the room, with North and West dark and South and East lit.
rows.note: The lit/dark Act 1 anchors are already wired (PR #12: `createActOnePortals` paints South and East lit, North and West dark) and the player capsule spawns at the room center. Traversal (`src/sim/portalTraversal.ts`) teleports the player to the destination spawn pose on lit-portal entry, defaulting to the room center via the pluggable `resolveSpawnPose` resolver. Still partial because the 5:00 timeline state itself (the time-of-day clock starting AT 5:00 normalized rather than at tick 0, and re-pinning to 5:00 on a return traversal) is not yet wired; the next slice authors per-time spawn poses and the 5:00 clock anchor.

rows.requirement: Door destinations from 5:00: South leads to 12:00 and East leads to 6:00.
rows.note: The destinations are authored in `ACT_ONE_PORTAL_SPECS` (PR #12: South to 12:00, East to 6:00) and `wireTraversal` reads `portal.destinationHours` via `portalDestinationNormalized` to drive both the player teleport's spawn pose lookup and the player's re-stamped `originNormalized` tint on traversal. So entering the South door at 5:00 now sends the player to 12:00 and entering the East door sends the player to 6:00, end-to-end. Still partial because the destination-side timeline state (the time-of-day clock pinning to 12:00 or 6:00 on arrival, and 6:00's West-only-lit configuration of REQ-015) is not yet wired; that flips REQ-014 to done alongside REQ-013 in the next slice.

rows.requirement: 6:00 timeline state: the room is empty, only the West door is lit, and the West door leads back to 5:00.
Act 2 first loop: traveling East then West produces a You-1 instance who replays You1's path, walks West, and disappears.
Act 2 second loop: knocking out You-1 on return to 5:00 and dragging the body East to 6:00 produces a You-2 instance who wakes and knocks out You1.
Act 3 setup: repeating the Act 2 sequence positions a knocked-out instance at 6:00 and the player waits for the other instance to wake.
Act 3 chase beat: running toward the West door while another instance chases pulls both instances through to 5:00 in the same frame.
Act 3 team-up beat: the two instances at 5:00 coordinate to knock out the 5:00 instance.
Act 3 mirror beat: dragging the knocked-out instance South to 12:00 and placing the body in the center of the room mirrors the Act 1 cinematic.
Act 3 second knockout: the player knocks out the instance brought from 6:00 inside the 12:00 timeline.
Act 3 escape: with no replay-instance staffing the North door cinematic, the North door at 12:00 is open and running through completes the level.
Beat dependency enforcement: acts cannot be executed out of order, and Act 3 requires the timeline state produced by Act 2.
Hard reset is available in the pause menu and returns the simulation to a clean Act 1 state.
Player spawn is keyboard-controllable in the room at 5:00.
rows.note: WASD/arrow keyboard movement on a Rapier dynamic capsule lands. The 5:00 timeline anchor is not yet wired (waits for the time-of-day clock from REQ-029).

rows.requirement: Four doors render in the scene, one per wall.
rows.note: Four door meshes render at the wall midpoints. Doors are visual-only; collisions and portal traversal land with REQ-001/REQ-005, and lit/dark state lands with REQ-028.

rows.requirement: Lit-versus-dark visual state of each door correctly reflects portal availability per the time travel rules.
Room color tints across a warm-to-cool spectrum over time.
rows.note: Warm-to-cool background tint is wired through a tick-locked TimeOfDay clock. Internal state is an integer `tickIndex` modulo `ticksPerCycle`, advanced once per fixed 60Hz physics step in `src/app.ts` via `advanceTicks(1)`. The same number of fixed steps always produces the same `normalized()` output, so timeline recording playback (REQ-001) and per-instance origin-time tints (REQ-030) can rely on it.

rows.requirement: Past instances tint to the room color at the time they last traveled, providing a visible timestamp.
rows.note: `applyInstanceTint(mesh, originNormalized)` stamps a capsule's material color with `interpolateWarmToCool(originNormalized)` at construction. The active player capsule receives the stamp at spawn from `TimeOfDay.normalized()`. Ghost capsules spawned via `createGhost(...)` carry an `originNormalized` derived from the recording's source timeline. Portal traversal (`src/sim/portalTraversal.ts`) now re-stamps the active player's tint and `originNormalized` to the destination's normalized time on every lit-portal entry via `applyInstanceTint(player.mesh, destinationNormalized)`, and tints the spawned ghost on the LIFETIME's origin (the timeline being left behind). Still partial because the system's notion of 'the time the instance last traveled' is currently a one-shot stamp on traversal rather than a per-frame mirror of the rendered timeline; a future per-timeline-rendering slice may revisit this row.

rows.requirement: The active player instance shows a subtle floor ring underfoot.
rows.note: `createFloorRing()` returns a Three.js RingGeometry mesh (inner 0.5, outer 0.7) with a low-opacity neutral white material, rotated flat onto the XZ plane and pinned to y=0.01 above the floor. `updateFloorRing(ring, body)` copies the body's planar translation onto the ring while keeping y pinned, so a jumping or falling player cannot drag the ring off the floor. `src/app.ts` adds the ring to the scene next to the player and updates it once per render frame after `player.syncMeshFromBody()`. The ring is intentionally neutral-toned (not warm-to-cool) because the GDD specifies it as the SOLE non-diegetic UI element. Multi-instance ring handoff (follow the most-recently-spawned active instance) lives with the slice that introduces multi-active-player semantics.

rows.requirement: Thought-bubble icons appear above past instances before key actions (door enter, fight, sleep).
Knockouts produce ragdoll physics on the receiving instance.
Unconscious bodies can be picked up by the player.
Unconscious bodies can be dragged across the room while held.
Unconscious bodies can be thrown through doors and travel to the door's destination time.
Demo build deploys to web with no install required.
Demo build loads in under 10 seconds on a typical broadband connection.
Demo build runs at 60fps on a 2020-era laptop.
Demo build supports the full Act 1 to Act 3 puzzle without crashes or timeline desync.
